title: Up/down-conversion of infrared light by few-layer graphene polytypes
authors: Patrick Johansen Sarsfield, Takaaki V. Joya, Takuto Kawakami, Mikito Koshino, Vladimir Falko
abstract: Optical nonlinearity of materials with broken inversion symmetry enables two-photon processes where an incoming pair of photons can generate an up-converted photon with the combined frequency, or a high-energy photon can be split into a correlated pair of down-converted photons. Here, we identify few-layer graphene films that offer up/down-conversion capability in the infrared spectral range. For mixed stacking tetralayers (ABCB), which are non-centrosymmetric 2D crystals, we find highly efficient nearly resonant up/down-conversion of [$ω_1,ω_2$] photon pairs into/from a photon with $0.7$eV$<Ω=ω_1+ω_2<1.1$eV. We also note that a pronounced second-order nonlinearity in the spectral range of $0.7$eV$<Ω<0.9$eV can be promoted in rhombohedral tri- and tetralayers by asymmetrical encapsulation. Potentially, for fibers coated with few-layer graphene, this opens the door for ``in fiber" production of photon pairs with correlated polarizations.
summary: This theoretical study predicts that few-layer graphene polytypes, particularly mixed stacking tetralayers, can efficiently mediate the up/down-conversion of infrared light. By calculating the second-order optical conductivity using advanced Green's function techniques, the authors pinpoint specific stacking orders and structural modifications that enhance this nonlinear process. This work suggests a pathway for creating correlated photon pairs in solid-state optical fibers.
main_problem: The study investigates the up/down-conversion of infrared light using few-layer graphene polytypes, focusing on second-order nonlinear optical phenomena.
main_result: Mixed stacking tetralayers (ABCB) are identified as highly efficient platforms for up/down-conversion in the infrared range, and asymmetrical encapsulation can promote nonlinearity in rhombohedral layers.
method: The authors used the Keldysh formalism for non-equilibrium Green’s functions to calculate the frequency-resolved second-order optical conductivity.
model_or_system: The system involves few-layer graphene films with various stacking orders (e.g., ABCB, rhombohedral). The theoretical framework includes an electron-photon interaction Hamiltonian leading to two-photon processes.
key_observables: Second-order optical conductivity ($\sigma_{aa}$), efficiency of up/down-conversion, and polarization correlations of generated photon pairs.
important_parameters: Photon energy ranges ($0.7 	ext{ eV} < \Omega < 1.1 	ext{ eV}$), stacking order (ABCB, rhombohedral), and external electric fields/encapsulation asymmetry.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the electronic structure is sensitive to the stacking sequence and that polarization correlations follow rules derived from $C_3$ symmetry.
figures_summary: Figures show color maps of the second-order conductivity for various stacking orders, illustrating resonance behavior and specific line cuts demonstrating expected double resonance pairs.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by deriving the necessary theoretical framework (Hamiltonian, Keldysh formalism), calculating the conductivity for different polytypes, and finally analyzing the resulting resonance maps and polarization selection rules.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses nonlinear quantum optics in solid-state materials, providing theoretical predictions for generating correlated photon pairs, which is highly relevant to quantum light sources and quantum information applications.
